findings.summary: The two new why-comments are attached to the wrong statements. The block at lines 32-34 ("Docling's markdown export HTML-escapes literal & < > ... unescape so the embedded text is human-readable ... resolve to real chars that replace_unicode_quotes then folds") describes html.unescape(text), but it precedes the comment-stripping regex on line 35 instead. The block at lines 36-38 ("Docling emits a <!-- image --> placeholder ... Strip all HTML comments BEFORE group_broken_paragraphs, which otherwise shreds them ... into noise") describes the re.sub(r"<!--.*?-->", ...) call, but it precedes html.unescape(text) on line 39 instead. Runtime behavior is unaffected today (both operations still run before replace_unicode_quotes and group_broken_paragraphs regardless of their order relative to each other), so this isn't a live bug, but the comment documenting the load-bearing 'must run before group_broken_paragraphs' ordering constraint is now attached to the wrong line, in a module whose own docstring stresses 'order matters'. A future edit that trusts the (wrong) comment and reorders based on it could reintroduce the exact shredding bug this change fixes.

findings.summary: The brief requires keeping table-structure detection on. The diff sets opts.do_ocr = False but never sets opts.do_table_structure, relying entirely on docling's PdfPipelineOptions default to satisfy that requirement (the inline comment asserts it's on, but nothing in the diff enforces it). A one-line opts.do_table_structure = True would make the brief's explicit requirement self-verifying in code instead of resting on an unstated, unpinned library default.
